root_idea.summary: A semantic field of preventing, withholding, and keeping apart.
root_idea.development: The root extends from abstract prohibition and debarment to concrete barriers, enclosures, confinement, and protection, including the maker of an enclosure.

senses.usage_conditions: Used of something made impermissible or barred.

senses.definition: Withheld or restricted, being confined to one class or group to the exclusion of others.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested use describing limited access or distribution rather than unrestricted availability.

senses.definition: One who makes an enclosure or fence.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic simile, the enclosure-maker is associated with the dry plant fragments collected or forming such an enclosure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To forbid, prohibit, or interdict something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prohibited object may be expressed directly or with عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To debar something from someone by means of an intervening barrier or obstruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes something being kept from a person by an intervening thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take something for oneself while withholding it from others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is explicitly explained as appropriation accompanied by exclusion of others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confine livestock in an enclosure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of enclosing or keeping cattle within a حَظِيرَة or حَظَار.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an enclosure for oneself or for another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The enclosure is a constructed حَظِيرَة; the use may be transitive with the beneficiary understood or expressed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mark off or assign separating limits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use for dividing or allotting an area by fixed boundaries; the evidence presents this meaning tentatively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To protect or defend oneself by means of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed figurative use with بِهِ or بِهَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trees used for making an enclosure, and fresh thorns used as enclosure material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote the physical plant material itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idiomatic expressions, a large number of cattle or people, and figuratively an odious lie, slander, or falsehood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In أتى أو جاء بالحَظِرِ الرَّطْبِ it may describe a large herd or crowd or, figuratively, offensive falsehood; kindling in the fresh-thorn enclosure denotes spreading calumny.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wall, enclosure wall, barrier, partition, obstruction, or fence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Denotes anything intervening between a person and a thing or between two things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enclosure or pen made of trees, wood, canes, or reeds, especially for confining and protecting livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of enclosures for camels, sheep, goats, and similar animals, including protection from cold and wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Paradise in the expression حَظِيرَةُ القُدْسِ.
A person of little or no good; figuratively, niggardly, tenacious, penurious, or avaricious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression نَكِدُ الحَظِيرَةِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which dates are dried.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal use reported for Najd; related variant forms are also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enclosure, in an alternative vocalization of the Quranic simile involving the dry fragments of an enclosure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is distinct from مُحْتَظِر, the maker of an enclosure, and reflects the alternative reading discussed for the expression at 54:31.
